original_description: Read a document (pasted text or a file) and check its verifiable factual claims — model specs, version numbers, pricing, statistics, API capabilities, release dates — against authoritative sources via live search, then report each as accurate, outdated (was true, now superseded), incorrect, or unverifiable, citing the source. Use when asked to fact-check a document, verify claims, check if info is still accurate/current, validate claims against official docs, confirm pricing or stats, or update stale data — even without the words "fact-check"/"verify," e.g. "is this still accurate," "check these numbers before I publish," "confirm this is backed by a real source." Always searches live instead of recalling from memory, never presents a guess as verified, proposes corrections with a citation, and asks approval before editing — never edits silently. Not for proofreading, style review, translation, or subjective content (opinions, architecture discussion, tutorial prose) — skips those.
